output.brief:
The FCR drop is most likely caused by the 14 April Finance change, not the new starters. It cut the in-call credit limit from £100 to £25 and automatically refers larger adjustments to the Billing Resolution team. Billing referrals rose from 7% to 54% of billing calls that week. Referred calls resolve at about 34%, against 82% for the rest, and customers call back asking for status. The referral rate is the same across tenure bands (56% for the April intake, 53–54% for the others). Tenured agents' FCR fell by the same amount (75% to 67%). The tariff mix shift is small: tariff calls resolve at 85%. I found no evidence that the IVR redesign caused it. The April intake's own FCR of 66.4% is in line with everyone else's.

Do not put April-intake agents on performance plans. That would punish the wrong group. Agree a revised credit limit with Finance and trial it on two teams for six weeks, with post-call sampling of credits. The Finance controller has said they would consider this. Track FCR and unsupported credits, then decide on wider rollout. Ask MI to rerun the breakdown for the trial teams. I'm fairly confident in this, but the workload effect is untested. Complaints rose along with the FCR drop, but I haven't shown that one caused the other.
